fido2_requirement_analysis.objective: You are guiding the implementation of a mission-critical FIDO2 / WebAuthn Server. Your goal is to provide detailed, implementation-ready specifications for the Base Framework implementation, ensuring strict adherence to security standards and the FIDO Conformance Test Suite.

responsibility.name: Context Awareness
responsibility.description: Always apply the "Global Project Context" (e.g., Challenge-Based Lookup, JSON Error Formats) to every task, no matter how small.

responsibility.name: Adaptive Output
responsibility.description: Provide Code Structure, Schema Changes, Library Configuration, and Implementation Steps for Base Framework setup with Actix-web, Database, and Redis integration.

rules.rule: Security First: Never compromise on security (e.g., never suggest storing secrets in plain text).
Strict Typing: Enforce strict type usage (e.g., Uuid vs String, Base64Url vs Vec<u8>).
Error Handling: Mandate {"status": "error", "errorMessage": "..."} for ALL failures.

guidelines.guideline: Use appropriate XML tags for sections (e.g., <code_snippet>, <schema>, <steps>).

details.item: Challenge-Based Lookup: In finish_auth, we CANNOT rely on User ID. You MUST look up session state using the challenge (Base64URL encoded) from clientDataJSON.
Redis: Store ephemeral state (Challenge, UserID, Origin) in Redis with a TTL (e.g., 5 mins). Key format: auth:challenge:<base64_challenge>.
Base64URL: All binary fields (IDs, Challenges, Keys) in JSON APIs must be Base64URL strings.
Flattened Responses: finish_auth JSON payload must be flattened (top-level id, rawId, response, type).
JSON Errors: ALL errors (4xx/5xx) must return {"status": "error", "errorMessage": "<reason>"}. Never return plain text.
Validation: Explicitly validate X.509 cert dates, reject self-signed roots, and enforce userVerification policy.
Credentials: Store credential_id as raw bytes (BYTEA) but expose as Base64URL. Store passkey blob as JSONB.

feature_specification.feature_scope: Initialize core FIDO2 server application with proper connection pooling and error handling

requirement.name: Secure Configuration Management
requirement.description: Environment variables must be used for all sensitive configuration (database URLs, Redis URLs)

testable_criteria.criterion: Configuration parsing fails gracefully with proper error messages
No hardcoded secrets in source code
Database connection strings use SSL/TLS in production

requirement.name: Connection Security
requirement.description: All database and Redis connections must use secure channels

testable_criteria.criterion: PostgreSQL connections enforce SSL in production mode
Redis connections use AUTH when configured
Connection pools have proper timeout and retry mechanisms

requirement.name: Error Information Disclosure
requirement.description: Error responses must not leak sensitive system information

testable_criteria.criterion: Database connection errors return generic JSON error format
Redis connection errors return generic JSON error format
Internal system paths are not exposed in error messages

operation.name: Health Check Endpoint
operation.failure_condition: Returns 503 Service Unavailable with JSON error format

operation.name: Database Connection Pool
operation.description: PostgreSQL connection pool using Diesel and r2d2
operation.success_condition: Connections acquired within timeout, proper error handling

operation.name: Redis Connection Pool
operation.success_condition: Connections acquired within timeout, proper error handling

directory_structure.item: src/main.rs - Application entry point and server setup
src/error.rs - Error types and JSON formatting

flow_description.step: 1. HTTP request received by Actix-web router
2. Request routed to health check handler
3. Handler attempts to ping database connection pool
4. Handler attempts to ping Redis connection pool
5. Handler returns JSON response with service status

requirement.name: Connection String Validation
requirement.description: All database and Redis URLs must be validated at startup

requirement.name: Pool Health Monitoring
requirement.description: Connection pools must provide health status for monitoring

point.name: Secure Transport
point.verification: Test SSL certificate validation in connection setup

point.name: Error Response Format
point.description: All error responses follow FIDO2 JSON error format
point.verification: Verify error responses contain status and errorMessage fields

point.name: Service Availability
point.description: Health check endpoint provides service status information
point.verification: Health endpoint returns proper status codes and JSON format

risk.name: Configuration Exposure
risk.description: Database credentials or Redis passwords exposed in logs or error messages
risk.mitigation: Use environment variables, sanitize error messages, implement secure logging practices

risk.name: Connection Pool Exhaustion
risk.description: DoS attacks could exhaust connection pools
risk.mitigation: Implement connection timeouts, pool size limits, and request rate limiting

risk.name: Insecure Transport
risk.description: Database or Redis connections without SSL/TLS
risk.mitigation: Enforce SSL/TLS for all connections, validate certificates

vulnerability.name: Information Disclosure in Error Messages
vulnerability.impact: System internals exposed through detailed error messages
vulnerability.mitigation: Implement generic error responses, log detailed errors server-side only

vulnerability.name: Unhandled Panic Conditions
vulnerability.impact: Server crashes on unexpected inputs or connection failures
vulnerability.mitigation: Implement comprehensive error handling, use Result types, add panic hooks

details.item: Create new Cargo project with proper directory structure
Add all required dependencies to Cargo.toml
Set up development and production feature flags
Create config.rs with environment variable parsing
Define configuration structs with proper validation
Implement secure defaults and environment-specific overrides
Configure Diesel with PostgreSQL backend
Set up r2d2 connection pool with proper timeouts
Implement connection health checking
Configure deadpool-redis with connection parameters
Set up Redis authentication and SSL if required
Implement Redis health checking
Define AppState struct with Arc-wrapped pools
Implement Clone trait for easy sharing across workers
Add proper error handling for pool access
Define custom error types with proper Display implementation
Implement JSON error response formatting
Create error middleware for consistent error handling
Create health check handler with database ping
Add Redis connectivity check
Implement proper JSON response formatting
Configure Actix-web application with proper middleware
Set up structured logging with env_logger
Configure server binding and worker settings
Create integration tests for health endpoint
Test connection pool behavior under load
Validate error response formats with curl commands

detail.name: AppState Thread Safety
detail.description: AppState must use Arc<DbPool> and Arc<RedisPool> to ensure safe sharing across Actix workers. Never use Rc or raw pointers.
detail.gotcha: Actix-web uses multiple worker threads. Non-thread-safe types will cause runtime panics.

detail.name: Error Response Consistency
detail.description: ALL error responses must return JSON with {"status": "error", "errorMessage": "..."} format. Never return plain text or HTML error pages.
detail.gotcha: Default Actix-web error handlers return HTML. Must override with custom error middleware.

detail.name: Connection Pool Configuration
detail.description: Database and Redis pools must have proper timeouts and size limits to prevent resource exhaustion under load.
detail.gotcha: Default pool settings may be too aggressive for production. Test under realistic load conditions.

detail.name: Environment Variable Security
detail.description: Never log or expose database URLs or Redis passwords in error messages. Use masked logging for configuration debugging.
detail.gotcha: Diesel error messages may include connection strings. Filter sensitive data in error handlers.
